visuals.title: Launch angle and range

limits: Level ground only; no drag. Original projectile kit remains the component-motion reference.

visuals.title: Horizontal launch from a height
visuals.focus: The vertical drop determines time; horizontal velocity determines range.
limits: One configured horizontal launch; not an obstacle solver or a full worked calculation.

visuals.title: Testing the projectile model
visuals.focus: A launcher and a graph connect measured drop to range squared.
visuals.entry: Horizontal launch model and graph axes

visuals.title: Force direction changes torque
visuals.focus: A perpendicular force produces the largest turning effect.
limits: Single-force comparison. Companion moment-arm and beam families supply the distance construction and force ledger.

visuals.title: Velocity turns while speed stays constant
visuals.focus: The inward net force continually changes the direction of velocity.
limits: Uniform circular motion only. Net force is not an extra force in a free-body diagram.

visuals.title: A banked track without friction
visuals.focus: The normal force supports weight and supplies the inward resultant.
limits: This family shows frictionless design speed. Companions cover conical motion and friction direction; limiting-speed derivations remain open.

visuals.title: Forces around a vertical loop
visuals.focus: Weight stays downward while tension points towards the centre.
visuals.entry: Energy conservation and radial force equations

visuals.title: Distance weakens the gravitational field
visuals.focus: Double the separation and the field falls to one quarter.
limits: Single spherical central mass outside its surface. Field-line density is not quantitative.

visuals.title: Compare circular orbital energies
visuals.focus: A higher circular orbit has lower speed and less negative total energy.
visuals.entry: Gravity provides radial net force; energy zero at infinity
limits: A parameter comparison, not an animated transfer manoeuvre. GEO synchronisation and orbit-transfer burns remain gaps.

visuals.title: Read a gravitational potential graph
visuals.focus: Potential rises towards zero as distance increases.

limits: The graph does not yet draw its tangent or show equipotential surfaces and work integrals.

visuals.title: Escape requires nonnegative total energy
visuals.focus: Compare kinetic, potential and total specific energy at one launch radius.
visuals.entry: Signed gravitational energy with zero at infinity
limits: Energy threshold only; no trajectory classification or relativistic escape models.

visuals.title: Equal times, equal swept areas
visuals.focus: An orbit speeds up near the central body and slows farther away.

visuals.title: Derive level-ground range

visuals.title: Clear a wall from a cliff
visuals.focus: Time at a horizontal location, then height against one datum

visuals.title: Two angles for one target

visuals.title: Repeated range measurements
